decision: Every prescribed merge route either invokes verify:pr-closeout-attestable (thin invoker over the existing evaluator) or names the control that closes the row. One evaluator, N thin invokers — cascade wait-mergeable and pr:merge-ready invoke in-process; human non-admin UI/CLI is named accident-only / open for first-ship (no CI required-check home chosen); local/push with no PR number is an explicit skip for orphan-active. Cascade --admin stays accident-closed via in-process invokers. Before closeout reads the tree, assert local HEAD equals the PR head SHA (exit 2 on mismatch).

governingRule.description: #3875 route-table Prefer-A; #3781 evaluator retained; #3156 gate integrity; #3265 thin fail-closed

alternativesConsidered.option: Keep #3781 single cascade call site and treat other routes as documentation-only
Add a pull_request required-check CI home in the same ship
Remove cascade --admin so required checks could cover admin merges

whyWinner: Drift across call sites is answered by one evaluator plus thin invokers, not by a single site. Human non-admin coverage must be named independently of an optional CI row; first-ship deliberately leaves CI unchosen and names that row accident-only while orphan-active keeps post-merge. Prefer-A keeps cascade --admin, so admin rows close against accident via in-process invokers rather than against an actor who wants through. HEAD/PR-head assert stops wrong-tree brief reads on every working-tree invoker.
revisitTrigger: If a CI pull_request required-check home is deliberately chosen, rename the human non-admin row to that check; if cascade --admin is removed, re-evaluate admin accident-close claims.
